chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinn (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah and Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari both narrated, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of al-'Ala' ibn Razin, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim, that I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'And pilgrimage to the House is incumbent upon men for the sake of Allah, (upon) everyone who is able to undertake the journey to it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should have the means to perform the pilgrimage.' I asked, 'What happens if someone offers to pay for your pilgrimage, and you feel embarrassed about accepting his offer?' He (peace be upon him) replied, 'Such a person would be counted among those who have the ability.'

key_terms.يَحُجُّ بِهِ: He performs Hajj with it (referring to means)

ai.seo_question: What constitutes 'ability' for Hajj if one is shy to accept financial help?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'ability' (istita'ah) for Hajj is defined by the possession of sufficient means, not merely the physical capacity to travel. The Imam further establishes that modesty or shyness in accepting financial support does not negate one's status as 'able,' thereby keeping the Hajj obligation firmly in place. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on objective financial capability over subjective hesitation when determining religious duties.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 10. My father and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (RA) both said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah and `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far al-Himyari both said, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, on the authority of al-`Ala’ ibn Razin, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: And pilgrimage to the House is incumbent upon men for the sake of Allah, (upon) everyone who is able to undertake the journey to it. He (AS) said: “He should have the means to perform the pilgrimage [hajj].” I asked, “What happens if someone offers to pay for your pilgrimage, and you fill embarrassed about accepting his offer?” He (AS) replied, “Such a person would be counted among those who have the ability (to perform the pilgrimage).”
